target: Saya merasa lelah sekali setelah rapat panjang tadi siang.
english: I feel really tired after the long meeting earlier this afternoon.
grammar: Merasa + a feeling word = to feel: saya merasa lelah = I feel tired.

target: Dia merasa nyaman tinggal di lingkungan yang tenang ini.
english: She feels comfortable living in this quiet neighborhood.

target: Kami merasa aman berjalan kaki di sekitar hotel pada malam hari.
english: We feel safe walking around the hotel at night.

target: Saya merasa bersalah karena lupa membalas pesan kamu kemarin.
english: I feel guilty because I forgot to reply to your message yesterday.
grammar: Bersalah = guilty, from salah (wrong): merasa bersalah = to feel guilty.

target: Setelah berolahraga pagi, badan saya terasa lebih segar.
english: After morning exercise, my body feels fresher.
grammar: People merasa; things terasa: badan saya terasa segar = my body feels fresh.

target: Anak baru itu masih merasa malu untuk bertanya di kelas.
english: That new student still feels shy about asking questions in class.

target: Saya sempat merasa canggung ketika bertemu mantan bos saya di lift.
english: I briefly felt awkward when I met my former boss in the elevator.

target: Nenek merasa kesepian sejak semua cucunya pindah ke luar kota.
english: Grandma has felt lonely since all her grandchildren moved out of town.

target: Setelah bercerita kepada kamu, saya merasa jauh lebih tenang.
english: After telling you about it, I feel much calmer.

target: Dia merasa dihargai karena idenya dipakai oleh tim.
english: He feels appreciated because his idea was used by the team.

target: Saya mulai merasa bosan dengan menu makan siang yang itu-itu saja.
english: I'm starting to feel bored with the same old lunch menu.
grammar: Itu-itu saja = the same old thing: menu yang itu-itu saja = the same old menu.

target: Kalau kamu merasa tidak enak badan, sebaiknya pulang lebih awal.
english: If you feel unwell, you should go home earlier.
grammar: Tidak enak badan = to feel unwell — literally 'body not nice'.

target: Saya merasa bahwa keputusan ini terlalu buru-buru diambil.
english: I feel that this decision was made too hastily.

target: Dia merasa kalau usahanya selama ini belum dihargai.
english: He feels that his efforts all this time have not yet been appreciated.
grammar: In speech, kalau often replaces bahwa after merasa: dia merasa kalau... = he feels that...

target: Kami merasa suasana kantor jauh lebih baik setelah pindah gedung.
english: We feel the office atmosphere is much better after moving buildings.

target: Saya merasa ada yang aneh dengan suara mesin mobil ini.
english: I feel something is odd about the sound of this car's engine.

target: Ibu merasa masakan hari ini kurang asin, bagaimana menurut kamu?
english: Mom feels today's cooking is not salty enough — what do you think?

target: Jujur saja, saya merasa harga sewa di daerah ini semakin tidak masuk akal.
english: Honestly, I feel rent prices in this area are getting more and more unreasonable.
grammar: Masuk akal = to make sense (literally 'enters reason'): tidak masuk akal = unreasonable.

target: Kelihatannya kamu kurang tidur, apakah semuanya baik-baik saja?
english: It looks like you haven't had enough sleep — is everything okay?
grammar: Kelihatannya = it looks like, built from lihat (see): kelihatannya kamu lelah.

target: Langit gelap sekali, kelihatannya sebentar lagi akan hujan deras.
english: The sky is very dark; it looks like it will pour very soon.

target: Kelihatannya dia senang sekali dengan hadiah ulang tahunnya.
english: It looks like she is really happy with her birthday present.

target: Dari wajahnya, kelihatannya kabar yang dia terima bukan kabar baik.
english: From his face, it looks like the news he received was not good news.

target: Restoran baru itu kelihatannya ramai terus setiap akhir pekan.
english: That new restaurant seems to be packed every weekend.

target: Kelihatannya proyek ini butuh waktu lebih lama dari rencana awal.
english: It looks like this project needs more time than the original plan.

target: Sepertinya saya pernah bertemu dengan dia, tetapi saya lupa di mana.
english: It seems I have met him before, but I forget where.
grammar: Sepertinya = it seems, from seperti (like): sepertinya dia sibuk = it seems he's busy.

target: Sepertinya kunci kamar saya tertinggal di dalam mobil.
english: It seems my room key was left behind in the car.

target: Dia tidak mengangkat telepon, sepertinya sedang sibuk.
english: She is not answering the phone; it seems she is busy.

target: Sepertinya rasa sup ini kurang garam, coba cicip dulu.
english: It seems this soup lacks salt — try tasting it first.

target: Sepertinya kita harus mencari jalan lain, jalan ini ditutup.
english: It seems we have to look for another road; this road is closed.

target: Sepertinya paket kamu baru akan sampai besok sore.
english: It seems your package will only arrive tomorrow afternoon.

target: Sepertinya musim hujan tahun ini datang lebih awal.
english: It seems the rainy season is coming earlier this year.

target: Kayaknya saya salah turun halte, ini bukan daerah yang saya cari.
english: Seems like I got off at the wrong stop; this is not the area I am looking for.
grammar: Kayaknya = colloquial 'seems like' — you will hear it everywhere; sepertinya is the neutral choice.

target: Kayaknya dia lupa dengan janji yang kita buat kemarin.
english: Seems like he forgot the promise we made yesterday.

target: Kayaknya akhir film ini sedih, saya sudah membawa tisu.
english: Seems like the ending of this movie is sad; I have already brought tissues.

target: Kayaknya enak kalau kita makan bakso hangat saat hujan begini.
english: Seems like it would be nice to have warm meatball soup in rain like this.
grammar: Kayaknya enak = 'that sounds nice' — a common way to float a food idea.

target: Kayaknya kamu cocok dengan gaya rambut yang baru itu.
english: Seems like that new hairstyle suits you.

target: Saya senang sekali karena akhirnya bisa bertemu kalian semua di sini.
english: I am really happy because I can finally meet all of you here.

target: Dia senang karena hasil ujiannya lebih baik dari yang dia kira.
english: She is happy because her exam result was better than she expected.

target: Kami senang karena tamu-tamu menikmati masakan buatan ibu.
english: We are glad because the guests enjoyed Mom's home cooking.

target: Anak-anak senang karena besok mereka libur sekolah.
english: The kids are happy because tomorrow they have a day off school.

target: Saya senang bekerja di sini karena rekan-rekan saling membantu.
english: I enjoy working here because my colleagues help each other.
grammar: Saling + verb = each other: saling membantu = help each other.

target: Dia sedih karena harus menjual motor kesayangannya.
english: He is sad because he has to sell his beloved motorbike.
grammar: Kesayangan = beloved/favorite, from sayang: motor kesayangannya = his beloved motorbike.

target: Kami sedih karena tetangga baik kami akan pindah ke kota lain.
english: We are sad because our kind neighbors are going to move to another city.

target: Saya ikut sedih mendengar kabar tentang kakek kamu.
english: I am also saddened to hear the news about your grandfather.
grammar: Ikut + feeling = to share it: saya ikut sedih = I'm sad for you too.

target: Dia kelihatan sedih sejak kucingnya hilang minggu lalu.
english: He has looked sad ever since his cat went missing last week.

target: Saya kecewa karena konsernya dibatalkan pada menit terakhir.
english: I am disappointed because the concert was canceled at the last minute.

target: Penonton kecewa karena tim favorit mereka kalah di babak final.
english: The spectators were disappointed because their favorite team lost in the final round.

target: Dia kecewa dengan pelayanan hotel itu, jadi menulis ulasan panjang.
english: She was disappointed with that hotel's service, so she wrote a long review.
grammar: Kecewa dengan = disappointed with: kecewa dengan pelayanan = disappointed with the service.

target: Jangan kecewa dulu, masih ada kesempatan lain tahun depan.
english: Don't be disappointed yet; there is still another chance next year.

target: Kami sedikit kecewa karena pemandangan dari kamar hotel tidak seindah foto di situs pemesanan.
english: We were a little disappointed because the view from the hotel room was not as beautiful as the photos on the booking site.
grammar: Se- + quality = as ... as: seindah foto = as beautiful as the photo.

target: Orang tuanya bangga karena dia lulus dengan nilai terbaik.
english: Her parents are proud because she graduated with the best grades.

target: Saya bangga pada tim ini karena kalian tidak pernah menyerah.
english: I am proud of this team because you all never gave up.
grammar: Bangga pada + person = proud of: bangga pada tim ini = proud of this team.

target: Dia bangga bisa membayar kuliahnya sendiri tanpa bantuan siapa pun.
english: He is proud that he could pay for his own college without anyone's help.

target: Kami bangga sekali karena kopi dari desa kami sekarang mulai dikenal di luar negeri.
english: We are very proud because coffee from our village is now starting to be known abroad.

target: Ibu selalu bilang dia bangga punya anak yang jujur.
english: Mom always says she is proud to have an honest child.

target: Ibu khawatir karena kakak belum pulang, padahal sudah hampir tengah malam.
english: Mom is worried because my older sibling is not home yet, even though it is almost midnight.
grammar: Padahal = even though / when in fact: belum pulang, padahal sudah malam.

target: Saya khawatir kita akan terjebak macet kalau berangkat siang.
english: I am worried we will get stuck in traffic if we leave at midday.

target: Dia khawatir tentang biaya rumah sakit ayahnya.
english: She is worried about her father's hospital costs.

target: Tidak usah khawatir, dokumen kamu sudah saya simpan di lemari.
english: No need to worry; I have already put your documents away in the cupboard.
grammar: Tidak usah = no need to: tidak usah khawatir = no need to worry.

target: Warga khawatir karena hujan deras sering membuat sungai meluap.
english: Residents are worried because heavy rain often makes the river overflow.

target: Saya berharap kamu bisa hadir di acara pernikahan kami bulan depan.
english: I hope you can come to our wedding next month.
grammar: Berharap needs a subject: saya berharap... Semoga opens a wish on its own: Semoga lancar!

target: Kami berharap harga bahan pokok tidak naik lagi tahun ini.
english: We hope the prices of basic goods will not rise again this year.

target: Dia berharap bisa mendapat beasiswa ke luar negeri tahun depan.
english: She hopes she can get a scholarship to go abroad next year.

target: Saya berharap hasil pemeriksaan besok tidak ada masalah serius.
english: I hope tomorrow's examination results show no serious problems.

target: Kami berharap kamu betah bekerja di kantor yang baru.
english: We hope you will feel at home working at the new office.
grammar: Betah = to feel at home somewhere: betah bekerja di sini = happy staying here.

target: Penduduk desa berharap jalan rusak itu segera diperbaiki pemerintah.
english: The villagers hope the damaged road will soon be repaired by the government.

target: Semoga acara besok berjalan lancar dari awal sampai akhir.
english: Hopefully tomorrow's event runs smoothly from start to finish.

target: Semoga keluarga kalian selalu diberi kesehatan dan rezeki.
english: May your family always be blessed with health and good fortune.
grammar: Rezeki = livelihood, blessings — a warm everyday wish word: diberi rezeki.

target: Semoga penerbangan kalian nyaman dan sampai dengan selamat.
english: Hope your flight is comfortable and you all arrive safely.
grammar: Sampai dengan selamat = arrive safely — the standard send-off for travelers.

target: Semoga masalah ini cepat selesai supaya kita semua bisa tenang.
english: Hopefully this problem is resolved quickly so we can all be at ease.

target: Semoga hujan berhenti sebelum kita harus berangkat ke stasiun.
english: Hopefully the rain stops before we have to leave for the station.

target: Semoga tahun ini usaha kecil kamu semakin berkembang.
english: Hopefully this year your small business grows more and more.
grammar: Semakin = more and more: semakin berkembang = growing more and more.

target: Saya lebih suka naik kereta daripada pesawat untuk perjalanan pendek.
english: I prefer taking the train to flying for short trips.
grammar: Lebih suka X daripada Y = to prefer X to Y: lebih suka kereta daripada pesawat.

target: Dia lebih suka bekerja pagi-pagi karena kantornya masih sepi.
english: He prefers working very early because his office is still quiet.

target: Kami lebih suka memasak sendiri daripada makan di luar setiap hari.
english: We prefer cooking ourselves to eating out every day.

target: Anak saya lebih suka membaca komik daripada buku pelajaran.
english: My child prefers reading comics to schoolbooks.

target: Untuk liburan, saya lebih suka gunung yang sejuk daripada pantai yang panas.
english: For vacations, I prefer cool mountains to hot beaches.

target: Ayah lebih suka kopi hitam tanpa gula, katanya lebih nikmat.
english: Dad prefers black coffee without sugar; he says it tastes better.
grammar: Katanya = he/she says, they say: katanya lebih nikmat = he says it tastes better.

target: Saya lebih suka rapat singkat di pagi hari daripada rapat panjang sore-sore.
english: I prefer short morning meetings to long late-afternoon meetings.

target: Dia lebih suka berbelanja di pasar karena bisa menawar harga.
english: She prefers shopping at the market because she can bargain over prices.

target: Kalau boleh memilih, saya lebih suka duduk dekat jendela.
english: If I may choose, I prefer sitting near the window.

target: Kakak lebih suka film komedi, sedangkan saya lebih suka film sejarah.
english: My older sibling prefers comedy films, while I prefer historical films.
grammar: Sedangkan contrasts two people or things: kakak suka komedi, sedangkan saya suka sejarah.

target: Tidak apa-apa datang terlambat, yang penting kamu datang dengan selamat.
english: It's fine to arrive late; the main thing is you arrive safely.
grammar: Yang penting = the main thing is: yang penting kamu selamat = what matters is you're safe.

target: Hasilnya belum sempurna, tetapi yang penting kita sudah mencoba.
english: The result is not perfect yet, but the main thing is we have tried.

target: Yang penting sekarang adalah kesehatan kamu, pekerjaan bisa menunggu.
english: The important thing right now is your health; work can wait.

target: Menang atau kalah, yang penting kalian bermain dengan jujur.
english: Win or lose, the main thing is you all play honestly.

target: Yang penting bagi saya, anak-anak tumbuh sehat dan bahagia.
english: What matters to me is that the kids grow up healthy and happy.

target: Rumahnya tidak besar, yang penting nyaman untuk keluarga kami.
english: The house is not big; the main thing is it's comfortable for our family.

target: Yang penting dokumennya lengkap dulu, sisanya bisa kita urus nanti.
english: The main thing is the documents are complete first; we can sort out the rest later.

target: Gajinya biasa saja, tetapi yang penting suasana kerjanya menyenangkan.
english: The salary is just average, but the main thing is the work atmosphere is pleasant.

target: Bagaimana menurut kamu, apakah warna ini cocok untuk ruang tamu?
english: What do you think — does this color suit the living room?
grammar: Bagaimana menurut kamu? = What do you think? — literally 'how according to you?'

target: Bagaimana menurut Anda tentang rencana perubahan jam kerja ini?
english: What is your opinion of this plan to change the working hours?
grammar: In formal settings (meetings, clients) use Anda instead of kamu: Bagaimana menurut Anda?

target: Bagaimana pendapat kalian tentang usul membuat jadwal piket baru?
english: What do you all think about the proposal to make a new duty roster?

target: Menurut saya, presentasi kamu tadi sudah jelas dan meyakinkan.
english: In my opinion, your presentation just now was clear and convincing.

target: Menurut saya pribadi, tempat wisata ini terlalu ramai untuk liburan keluarga yang tenang.
english: Personally, I think this tourist spot is too crowded for a calm family holiday.

target: Kalau menurut saya, kita sebaiknya menunda dulu pembelian mobil itu.
english: In my opinion, we had better postpone buying that car for now.

target: Saya setuju dengan pendapat kamu tentang pentingnya istirahat cukup.
english: I agree with your opinion about the importance of getting enough rest.

target: Saya kurang setuju kalau semua rapat dipindahkan ke hari Jumat.
english: I don't quite agree with moving all the meetings to Friday.
grammar: Kurang setuju softens disagreement — politer than a flat tidak setuju.

target: Maaf, saya berbeda pendapat soal cara membagi tugas ini.
english: Sorry, I have a different opinion about how to divide these tasks.
grammar: Berbeda pendapat = to disagree — literally 'to differ in opinion'.

target: Sebagian teman setuju, sebagian lagi menolak rencana itu.
english: Some friends agree; some others reject the plan.
grammar: Sebagian ... sebagian lagi = some ... others: sebagian setuju, sebagian lagi menolak.

target: Dia jarang berpendapat di rapat, tetapi idenya selalu bagus.
english: He rarely gives his opinion in meetings, but his ideas are always good.

target: Sebelum memutuskan, kita perlu mendengarkan pendapat semua anggota.
english: Before deciding, we need to listen to the opinions of all the members.

target: Menurut pengalaman saya, pelanggan lebih suka jawaban yang jujur.
english: In my experience, customers prefer honest answers.

target: Jangan takut menyampaikan pendapat, di sini semua ide dihargai.
english: Don't be afraid to voice your opinion; here every idea is appreciated.
grammar: Menyampaikan pendapat = to voice an opinion, from sampai (reach).

target: Menurut kamu, lebih baik kita berangkat malam ini atau besok pagi?
english: What do you think — is it better to leave tonight or tomorrow morning?

target: Saya menghargai pendapat kamu, tetapi kali ini saya punya cara sendiri.
english: I appreciate your opinion, but this time I have my own way.

target: Setelah mendengar pendapat kalian, saya jadi lebih yakin dengan pilihan ini.
english: After hearing all of your opinions, I feel more confident about this choice.

target: Pendapat kita memang berbeda, tetapi saya yakin kita tetap bisa bekerja sama dengan baik.
english: Our opinions do differ, but I am sure we can still work together well.

target: Menurut warga sekitar, pasar malam itu paling ramai hari Sabtu.
english: According to the local residents, that night market is busiest on Saturdays.

target: Terima kasih atas masukan kalian, semua akan kami pertimbangkan.
english: Thank you for your input; we will consider all of it.
grammar: Masukan = feedback/input, from masuk (enter): terima kasih atas masukan kalian.

target: Kabar baik itu membuat kami lega setelah menunggu berminggu-minggu.
english: That good news made us relieved after waiting for weeks.
grammar: Membuat + person + feeling = to make someone feel: membuat kami lega = made us relieved.

target: Saya terharu melihat murid-murid menyiapkan kejutan untuk guru mereka.
english: I was touched to see the students preparing a surprise for their teacher.

target: Dia puas dengan hasil renovasi rumahnya walaupun biayanya besar.
english: He is satisfied with the result of his house renovation even though the cost was high.

target: Awalnya saya ragu, tetapi sekarang saya yakin keputusan ini benar.
english: At first I was unsure, but now I am sure this decision is right.
grammar: Awalnya = at first, from awal (beginning): awalnya saya ragu = at first I was unsure.

target: Suasana hati saya langsung membaik setelah mendengar suara anak-anak.
english: My mood improved instantly after hearing the children's voices.
grammar: Suasana hati = mood — literally 'atmosphere of the heart'.

target: Dia berusaha tetap sabar walaupun antreannya panjang sekali.
english: She tries to stay patient even though the queue is very long.

target: Kami kaget mendengar harga tanah di daerah ini naik dua kali lipat.
english: We were shocked to hear that land prices in this area have doubled.
grammar: Dua kali lipat = double: naik dua kali lipat = doubled.

target: Setiap kali gugup, dia menarik napas panjang supaya lebih tenang.
english: Every time he gets nervous, he takes a deep breath to feel calmer.

target: Perasaan saya campur aduk antara senang dan sedih pada hari terakhir saya bekerja di sini.
english: My feelings were all mixed up between happy and sad on my last day working here.
grammar: Campur aduk = all mixed up: perasaan campur aduk = mixed feelings.

target: Jangan pendam perasaan kamu sendirian, ceritakan kepada orang terdekat.
english: Don't bury your feelings alone; tell someone close to you.

target: Saya kagum pada semangat kerja tim kecil ini.
english: I admire the working spirit of this small team.

target: Dia bersemangat sekali menceritakan rencana pernikahannya kepada kami.
english: She was very enthusiastic telling us about her wedding plans.

target: Pelan-pelan rasa takutnya hilang setelah dia mencoba berenang lagi.
english: Little by little his fear disappeared after he tried swimming again.
grammar: Pelan-pelan = little by little: pelan-pelan rasa takutnya hilang.

target: Menurut saya, jujur tentang perasaan lebih baik daripada diam saja.
english: In my opinion, being honest about feelings is better than just staying silent.

target: Apa pun pendapat orang, keluarga kami tetap bangga pada pilihan kamu.
english: Whatever people's opinions, our family remains proud of your choice.
grammar: Apa pun = whatever / no matter what: apa pun pendapat orang = whatever people think.
